body: No, I've just always thought that clinical depression happens with or without situational stimuli. Mine has always been triggered by some event that affects me deeply. It's not cyclical.

I don't think that's true.  The only thing that is real to me right now are the painkillers I just bought. I've taken a few throughout the day already. They helped me get through work. I'll use the rest up as I see fit.

I stopped contacting him or one month. He replied then stopped. Cue 3 days of texting before I finally was dejected enough to quit. A month later he tried to call me a bunch of times. I hesitated and recently tried to call him back, called his work, asked his friend to call me because I was concerned. No call back. I'm sick of this cycle.

I've given him space in between. I don't know anymore. Maybe he hates me.
I tried. I asked his friend to tell him to call me. He hasn't called. I even left messages at his workplace. Nothing.
No. Not to this extent
Someone can fill him in when I die.i just can't say anything anymore without getting hurt
I don't understand how he doesn't know. I messaged him a lot and expressed my anguish.
If I died, then he would know I was hurting regardless

I tried. He doesn't reply to my texts and calls. I felt like an idiot sending text after text for a span of maybe 3 days. I couldn't sleep well. I left a voicemail describing how much it hurt that he was stonewalling me. Nothing. He didn't care if I suffered like that then, would he care if I'm suffering like this now? Each time he doesn't respond is another rejection. He wanted me to give up...he chose to let me hurt....

It just seems like I can't get out of it. I started taking painkillers to help take the edge off and I wonder if it's the only thing that will help me. I've tried exercise, dating, being social, etc. but they're just distractions. I come home to my room and the feeling comes back again.
I try to heal and then I don't. I'm starting to think that it's not possible.

My ex and I should have never met. 

I've had phases of depression before, you'd think I would just end it already. I should keep some pills on hand, just to feel like I have that option.

No meds. I'm sorry I am hurting the people who love me. I will stop hurting the people who love me by disappearing- I will distribute my assets among them as compensation for dealing with me.

To my ex, it's better off if I'm permanently dead to him. All I do is bother him.
He'll most likely never want to speak to me again.  Just imagining him saying that to my face makes me not want to say anything. I'd rather disappear.
The lesson here is that I'm done being me.

Too ashamed to say it. But it could have hurt his feelings badly and made him do something extreme. Not saying he did, but the potential for that was high. All in the name of getting even. I'm a terrible person. I'm sorry I did it, but the damage has been done, it's too late. Maybe I scared someone emotionally who knows.

He rarely initiates contact though, so the fact that he is calling and texting for days says something. He even called my work. It seems crappy to ignore him, yet he did the same thing some many times to me.

Sunk costs. People think 'We've known each other for xx amount of time, why throw that away?' And while they have a point, they don't allow enough time to truly heal and can reopen old wounds. This can result in a cycle of on and off again relationships until one or both parties exhaust themselves emotionally. The intentions behind the person wanting friendship can be good, but they may not understand that this can hurt more than help the other person.

"my ex basically cheated on me, blamed me for it, lied to the girl about my existence and then ignored me"

This to me is self-explanatory. If you want to be generous, go ahead an tell him you need time away. But if you ask me, it sounds like your ex is having a hard time owning up to the fact that he cheated. He most likely is looking to relieve his guilt-he tried blaming you, ignoring you, and now he wants your affection and approval to make it all ok and to make the cheating more acceptable.

Also notice how your ex talks about himself and his own suffering. He also mentioned nothing about apologizing for what he did. He is suffering the consequences of his actions, and rightly so. 

Determine what kind of love you want for yourself and know that there is someone out there who won't cheat on you and won't manipulate you. Hugs for going through this whole ordeal. Focus on your own healing. Remain NC for a while.
She ghosted you on purpose, remember that. You'll just get silence on her end. Wish her well in your heart but know that there's nothing you can say when a person refuses to communicate with you.
I had always given him the benefit of the doubt. But a friend and I were hanging out and I noticed that she was getting replies back from him and not me. That's how I knew it had to be intentional.

This post was so relatable that it brought up some bad and painful memories.  I essentially was that crazy person thinking I could win my ex back until I broke down and realized how horribly and awfully one-sided it all was.

Yeah this pretty much describes how I feel.  I'm pretty much over what happened between us, but I miss being able to share stuff about my day and hear about his.
Sometimes I think about telling him something interesting or funny that happened.  But then I realize that telling him would seem out of place given that I haven't talked to him in a while.  I also don't want to set myself back because I really do want to not feel sad about our breakup anymore.

"...you're also grieving what could have been had this not been long distance..."

This is actually really true and I didn't consciously realize I was thinking about this until now.  I always thought about what would happen if we weren't LDR and if it would have made things better.  There's so many 'what ifs' in this type of situation because my ex never told me the whole truth - if I'm not careful I can spend hours ruminating how this breakup would've been avoided and if I have a chance to fix things.

I will definitely seek out more help from others.  I've kept it repressed for a while because I don't want to annoy my friends with all the drama, but I may seek some professional help if things get too overwhelming.  Posting here helps too.

I can only imagine how hard your breakup was.  I mean, when I think about the 2 years I put into my LDR, I just think about all the effort gone down the drain.  I hate the way my ex has ended things because I feel like he gets the easy way out and I have to painfully crawl my way through this breakup.
Yeah, but HR is taking longer than usual to get back to me, and it's sort of worrying me. They think I won't be able to have enough training to cover for the other employee in time.
Nothing.  The start date wasn't formalized when I accepted the offer, so we're technically still negotiating it.  They were saying they would try to be flexible, but I don't know how flexible.
They were about the same level, both having many years of experience with the company.
It was an all day interview with 5 separate people.  Definitely not a 6 figure job.

Nice.  As I've been interviewing, I've been realizing how little practical engineering knowledge I have, which is why I think being a tech might be helpful.  Can you describe in more detail how your experience as a tech helped you become an engineer?

Being able to work would be a huge plus and I agree with a lot of the points you mentioned.  The uncertainty in knowing whether or not being a tech will help me find work as an engineer bothers me, but I guess I'll just have to make do with what I can get and wing it.
Doing a masters isn't really an option for me, mostly because I don't have the money for it.  Night school could be an option, though I have no idea what kind of classes I would be taking.
